predecessors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
predecessors.text: the ethnically Polish lands ceded to France by Prussia under the Treaties of Tilsit (7 and 9 July 1807): New East Prussia, Southern Prussia, New Silesia and West Prussia (the Land of Chełmno)

successors.name: Kingdom of Prussia
successors.text: the western territories 'reconstituted into the Grand Duchy of Posen' (Greater Poland, the Bromberg district) and the Chełmno Land, which 'became part of the Province of West Prussia'

successors.name: Free City of Kraków
successors.text: Kraków, made a 'semi-independent Free City of Cracow'

successors.name: Russian Empire
successors.text: the bulk of the duchy, 're-established as' the Congress Kingdom of Poland under the Russian emperor

ledger.x: 1807: Napoleon creates the Duchy of Warsaw from the Polish lands taken from Prussia.
July 1807: the duchy is a French satellite from its creation.
April 1809: with the Austrians invading, the seat moves to Toruń.
June 1809: the capital returns to Warsaw.
14 October 1809: Schönbrunn gives the duchy West Galicia.
January 1813: the French hold ends with the Russian occupation.
9 June 1815: the Congress of Vienna ends the occupation by partitioning the duchy.
9 June 1815: the western lands go back to Prussia.
1815: Kraków becomes the 'semi-independent Free City of Cracow'.
1815: the bulk of the duchy becomes the Congress Kingdom of Poland under the Russian emperor.
1815: the Duchy of Warsaw is dissolved.

wars.name: Austro-Polish War
wars.outcome: Treaty of Schönbrunn, 14 October 1809: Austria cedes Lublin, Kraków, Siedlce and the Zamość district to the duchy, and Tarnopol to Russia; West Galicia is incorporated into the duchy.

wars.name: French invasion of Russia
wars.outcome: The duchy joined the invasion (infobox: '24 June 1812'; on 28 June the Sejm formed the General Confederation of the Kingdom of Poland); Russia occupied most of the duchy in January 1813.

certainty.note: The Tilsit (1807) and Schönbrunn (14 October 1809) treaties fixed the frontiers but the pages give departments and area, not boundary lines; the outline is Cliopatria's approximation.
